item.title: China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council have issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development. The guidelines outline 19 key measures in five areas, including advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, innovating development approaches, promoting institutional and mechanism innovation, and improving mechanisms for talent development. Noting that developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development, the guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old." The document calls for pursuing high technology, high efficiency and high quality, properly handling the relationships between the government and the market, between the qualitative nature of productive forces and the forms they take in industry and business, between reform and development, and between self-reliance and opening up, while coordinating development and security.

item.title: China warns Philippines over Ren'ai Reef provocation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
China Coast Guard has warned the Philippines to cease conducting infringing provocations and stop making false narratives, its spokesman said in a statement on Thursday night. Jiang Lue said Philippine Coast Guard vessel 4409 approached waters near Ren'ai Reef to collect an injured crew member from an illegally "grounded" ship there. For humanitarian reasons, China promptly allowed the Philippines to use small boats for the transfer. China Coast Guard handled the situation in accordance with the law and provided necessary assistance, Jiang said. "However, the statements from the Philippine side disregard the facts and distort the truth, attempting to mislead public opinion," he said. "China holds indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha Islands, including Ren'ai Reef, and the surrounding waters. We sternly warn the Philippine side to immediately cease their infringing provocations and false narratives."

item.title: 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA sets off for helicopter rotation mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
By Huang Hao, Wu Xinwei, Pei Gaofeng and Bi Sheng Members of the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA inspect a helicopter. ABYEI, Oct. 9 -- Two helicopters of the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) departed from the UNISFA Smart Camp in Abyei on October 6, 2026, heading to Entebbe International Airport in Uganda for a rotation mission under UN's deployment. As a key and highly demanding annual cross-border task for the Chinese contingent, the mission is critical to updating the air forces in the mission area, sustaining regular patrol capabilities, and maintaining stability in the Abyei region. Members of the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA install an auxiliary fuel tank on a helicopter. Pilots assigned to the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA report to the control tower prior to takeoff. A helicopter of the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Helicopter Contingent to UNISFA takes off for arotation mission.

item.title: AI should not be used to distort historical truth or whitewash Japan's wartime aggression
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
AI should be used for good and to advance human progress, not to distort historical truth or whitewash Japan's wartime aggression, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Friday. The remarks were made after reports show that Japanese right-wing forces have been feeding major international AI models falsified historical data on WW II, leading some models to generate responses reflecting a clearly distorted view of history, including examples like referring to the Marco Polo Bridge Incident as a "Sino-Japanese military conflict," downplaying the Nanjing Massacre as the "Fall of Nanjing," and whitewashing Japan's invasion of Southeast Asia as "concern for southern resources." The evidence of Japan's militarist aggression is irrefutable and cannot be denied. Using new technologies to "poison" data is a new tactic employed by Japan's right-wing forces to distort and whitewash its history of aggression, with the aim to distort global public understanding of WW II history and clear public opinion hurdles for Japan to break free from the constraints of the postwar order and accelerate its "remilitarization," Mao said. The underhanded and malicious maneuvers by Japan's right-wing forces seriously hurt the feelings of the people of countries that suffered from Japanese aggression and constitute a blatant affront to human conscience. The international community must remain vigilant and work together to resist such efforts, Mao stated.

item.title: Chinese FM rejects Philippine claims about disruptions of medical evacuation near Ren'ai Jiao
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson on Friday rejected Philippine claims about disruptions of a medical evacuation from a Philippine vessel illegally grounded at China's Ren'ai Jiao, stressing China will firmly respond to any malicious provocation and resolutely safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks on Friday, reiterating that a Philippine coast guard vessel had entered waters near Ren'ai Jiao in China's Nansha Qundao without China's permission on Thursday morning. The measures taken by the China Coast Guard (CCG) in accordance with laws and regulations were justified and reasonable, Mao said. Following communication between the two sides, China promptly allowed the injured person to be transferred by a small boat on humanitarian grounds and provided necessary assistance, Mao added. Instead of showing appreciation, some individuals in the Philippines disregarded the facts, took information out of context and shifted blame onto China, Mao said. This again exposed their real intention of stirring up trouble and seeking attention, she said, calling such conduct disgraceful. Mao's remarks followed a statement issued on Thursday evening by CCG spokesperson Jiang Lue, who said Philippine coast guard vessel 4409 had traveled to waters near Ren'ai Jiao that day to evacuate an injured person from the Philippine warship illegally grounded there. Jiang also confirmed that out of humanitarian considerations, the Chinese side immediately allowed the Philippine side to transfer the injured person by small boat, and the CCG handled the matter in accordance with the law and regulations, and provided necessary assistance. Jiang said the Philippine side's remarks disregarded the facts, distorted the truth and sought to mislead the public. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao, including Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, he said, warning the Philippine side to immediately stop its infringements, provocations and dissemination of false claims.
